title: Condition a shared contractive equilibrium operator with Mirror codes
hypothesis: For four 2D fixed-point functions generated from one contractive shared map, a per-context Givens Mirror code reaches independent-operator normalized equilibrium RMSE within 10% at <=60% actual payload bytes, with all code solves converging and no increase in iterations.
physical_object: one shared recurrent equilibrium map z <- tanh(Az + Bx)
mirror_coordinate: one context-specific Givens angle conjugating the shared recurrent matrix A

task.teacher: z*=tanh(Q_c A Q_c^T z* + Bx), with spectral norm A <=0.6

development.selection_metric: lowest validation equilibrium normalized RMSE among convergent codes

training.projection: project each learned recurrent operator to spectral norm <=0.8 after update

success_gate: Every fresh Mirror context converges; Mirror mean NRMSE <=1.1x independent, actual bytes <=60% independent, and max solve iterations no greater than independent.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality/storage/solver stability gates, or simple scalar/rank-one control dominates at comparable bytes.
boundaries: Teacher generated by a rotated shared operator; aligned feasibility only.
Small 2D system with spectral projection; high-dimensional DEQ behavior is untested.
Fixed-point regression, not language model quality.
